text.content:
The medieval understanding of madness holds that it comes from one of three sources: possession, divine insight, or condemnation. These three optional Archetypes reflect that trinity of dementia for Malkavian characters. They are a starting point rather than a restriction — every other Archetype remains open to a Madman — but each offers a distinct lens for portraying a Malkavian's divine lunacy and a distinct trigger for regaining spent Willpower.

  • Seer: An oracle, prophet, or poet of Clan Malkavian, gifted (or cursed) with sight and awareness that lets her see past deceptions and glimpse a fluctuating understanding of past and future. To others she seems detached and otherworldly, which is why they seek her counsel and also why they fear her. Regain Willpower whenever you shed light on a mystery or enigma, or grant someone else a greater understanding of themselves, their world, or their actions.
  • Maniac: You hear voices, not out in the darkness but inside you, and they are all you can hear. Sometimes benevolent, sometimes vile and tempting, they are only silenced when you submit to them; in time your own voice is lost in their cacophony as a new, possessing personality emerges. Regain Willpower whenever you fulfill a goal of your inner voice(s) that runs contrary to your immediate self-interest.
  • Melancholic: Once you stood at the threshold between life and death and glimpsed the face of God; then, in a single painful moment, the light seeped away and left only darkness and madness. You are a harbinger and prophet of doom, certain that you and all Cainites are forsaken, yet you cling to a single glimmer of hope that redemption remains possible for those who acknowledge their sins. Regain Willpower whenever your actions cause others to question their own cursed and damned natures.
